analysis:
Both units are CHANGELOG.md head-text excerpts (lines 2176-2634) holding historical release notes for v0.10.1 through v0.10.3 and the tail of the add-on hold sections. This PR's actual change is a documentation addition at the top of the file (v0.10.9 candidate notes, head lines 11-400). No source code, protocol, crypto, or config files are in these units, so no behavior changes in them.

Security-relevant content in the excerpts is descriptive and consistent with the threat model. It covers the TB-012 add-on hold hardening (signer verified before an accept slot is consumed, 10s request-line bound, FIFO refusal on the hold record and mailbox files, model-load fence), mapping to T-059 and T-060. It covers prefix-cache SSD checkpoint changes (4-bit balanced checkpoints, new namespaces, TTL sweep), mapping to T-041. It also notes that log lines for refusals never contain request text, and that the desktop control API is loopback and authenticated. Nothing in the text weakens a stated mitigation, such as the 30-minute TTL, HMAC lookup tags, or account-scoped cache salts. Some entries note changed on-disk layouts that expire via the normal TTL sweep, which is consistent with T-041.

Limits: the excerpts are only parts of the changelog. The patch excerpt is truncated, and the v0.10.9 section (head lines 11-400) was not in the supplied units, so it is not assessed here. The underlying code claims cannot be verified from changelog prose. The new v0.10.9 notes should be checked in a pass that sees that section, if any other batch covers it.
